title: Teratogenic Effects of Serotonin Receptor 2B Disruption on the Migration and Cardiac Derivatives of the Cardiac Neural Crest
abstract: Cardiac neural crest cells (cNCCs) are critical for heart development, and their disruption can result in congenital heart defects. Serotonin (5‐HT) signaling, specifically via 5‐HT2B and 5‐HT2C receptors, regulates diverse physiological processes, including neural crest migration. This study investigates how modulation of 5‐HT2B and 5‐HT2C receptor activity impacts cNCC migration and the development of their derivatives, with relevance to serotonergic drug safety during pregnancy.
